- **Birth year — 1870 census:** The 1870 census [F] implies **1840–1841**, conflicting with six other sources that converge on 1838–1839. This is likely a census enumeration error; re-reading the original 1870 image would clarify whether the indexed age was misread.

These are genuinely different names. Possible explanations: Joseph Tallman married twice (Hannah first, then Jane Patterson as stepmother), or the 1850 indexer misread the name. **Weaknesses:**
- The specific birth day and month (30 Nov) rest on no traceable primary source and conflict with Find a Grave.
- The first marriage (to Mary) has no tagged source despite direct census evidence.
- Neither marriage has a tagged source or a complete date.
- All five residence conclusions are untagged.

## Annotations

### 1. Conflicting Evidence Between Sources

**Birth date — month and day conflict (Find a Grave vs. profile).**
The profile records 30 November 1838 as the birth date. The only source that gives a full day-month-year is the Find a Grave Index [J], which indexes 31 January 1839. The two dates share neither the month, the day, nor the year. No other source provides a day or month — the death records and census records yield only year ranges derived from age. Find a Grave entries typically reproduce dates entered by memorial contributors from family tradition or secondary sources, not from primary vital records. Neither date can be verified against a primary document from this audit alone. The original birth registration or a family bible would be needed to settle which (if either) is correct. Since this profile's month and day appear to come from a source not among those FamilySearch's index surface here, they should be traced to their origin before being treated as established.

**Birth year — 1870 census vs. all other sources.**
The 1870 census [F] implies a birth year in the range 1840–1841, two to three years later than the range 1838–1839 that the death records, 1850 census, 1865 census, 1910 census, and Vermont vital records all support. This is the conflict FamilySearch's own quality check flags. A two-to-three-year gap in a census age is at the outer edge of ordinary enumeration variance; the weight of the other sources argues for the 1838–1839 range. Re-reading the original 1870 census page would clarify whether the indexed age was misread.

**Birth year — 1880 census.**
The 1880 census [H] implies a range of 1839–1840, one year later than the profile's year. This is ordinary census variance and is not a conflict.

**Father's name — "Jas" vs. "Joseph".**
Vermont Vital Records 1760-1954 [K] indexes the father as "Jas Tallman." In 19th-century handwriting, "Jos." (Joseph, abbreviated) and "Jas." (James, abbreviated) look very similar. The 1850 census [D] unmistakably identifies the father of this household as Joseph Tollman, not James. Vermont Vital Records 1760-2008 [B] indexes the father as "Joo Tallman," which is almost certainly another misread of "Jos." Both [B] and [K] are probably indexing the same underlying death registration (the Vermont death certificate for 16 August 1913), and both represent the same transcription challenge. The two records should not be treated as independent evidence of two different fathers.

**Mother's name — Hannah vs. Jane Patterson.**
The 1850 United States Census [D] lists the head of household as Joseph Tollman (b. 1804, Canada) and his wife as Hannah Tollman (b. 1812, Canada). All three Vermont death records and vital record entries that give a mother's name ([A], [B], [K]) name her as Jane Patterson. These are not the same name. Two explanations are possible: Joseph Tallman was married twice — once to a Hannah (Edward's birth mother, as recorded in 1850) and once to a Jane Patterson (Edward's stepmother, whose name may have been reported at his death) — or the 1850 census indexer misread the first name (this is less likely, as Hannah and Jane look nothing alike in script). This is a genuine conflict requiring further research; it cannot be resolved from these sources alone.

**Death place — varying precision.**
The Vermont Town Clerk record [C] gives the death place as "Vermont" only. Vermont Vital Records 1760-1954 [K] gives "Burlington, United States" (omitting the state and county). Both are less precise than the profile's "Burlington, Chittenden, Vermont, United States," which is fully supported by [A] and [B]. These are precision gaps in the indexes, not contradictions; the more specific values from [A] and [B] appear to represent the same event.

**Two marriages — sources and sequence.**
The profile records two marriages, neither with tagged sources and neither with a complete date. The 1865 New York State Census [E] is the only source read that directly evidences the first marriage, naming wife Mary Tallman (b. 1841) and a daughter Lilly (b. 1865) in the same household. The 1870 census [F] shows no wife in Edward's immediate entry. By 1875 [G], Clarissa Tollman (Clarissa Wade) is in the household. This pattern is consistent with Mary dying between 1865 and 1870 and Edward marrying Clarissa Wade before 1875. However, neither marriage event has a date with a month, and neither has a tagged source.

**Surname indexing error — source [A].**
Vermont, Deaths and Burials, 1871-1965 [A] indexes Edward's surname as "Mollman." All other sources — including two other Vermont vital record indexes of what appears to be the same underlying death event — index it as "Tallman" or "Tollman." The surrounding context in [A] is otherwise consistent: same death date, same death place, same father's first name, same mother's name, same spouse's name. This is an indexing error in [A], not a misattribution; the record is about the right person.

---

### 2. Patterns in Consistent Evidence

**Death date.** Five independent sources — [A], [B], [C], [J], [K] — all index 16 August 1913 as the death date. This is the most strongly evidenced conclusion on the profile.

**Death place (Burlington, Chittenden, Vermont).** Two of those five — [A] and [B] — give the full hierarchy down to Chittenden County. The others are less precise but consistent. Burlington, Chittenden, Vermont is well supported.

**Birth year range 1838–1839.** Six sources converge on this range: the death record age [A], the 1850 census age [D], the 1865 census age [E], the 1910 census age [I], and two Vermont vital records [J, K]. The 1880 census extends the range one year to 1840 (tolerable variance). Only the 1870 census stands materially outside it.

**Parents — father Joseph, mother Jane Patterson.** Three sources ([A], [B], [K]) all name Jane Patterson as mother, and two of those plus the 1850 census ([A], [D], and by inference [K]) identify the father as Joseph. The Joseph identification is strong.

**Spouse 2 — Clarissa Wade.** Three sources ([A], [G], [L]) independently confirm Edward's marriage to Clarissa Wade/Tollman across three different record types (a death registration, a state census, and a vital record for a daughter). This is well supported.

**Children from Clarissa.** The 1875 and 1880 censuses together confirm several children: Frances/Francis, Nellie, Phebe, Blanch/Blanche, Theodore, Norah, and Orrin. Phoebe appears in 1910 as married to a Derby and living in Monroe County, NY. Helen McIntosh's 1943 death record identifies her as a daughter.

---

### 3. Conclusions with No Supporting Evidence or Only One Weak Source

**Birth day and month (30 November 1838 or any specific date).** No source independently confirms a specific day and month. The profile value does not come from any source readable in this audit. The Find a Grave Index [J] gives a full date (31 January 1839) but it is a single secondary source, and the day and month on a Find a Grave entry may originate from a memorial contributor's family information rather than a primary document.

**Both marriage events.** Neither marriage has a tagged source on the profile. The 1865 census [E] is direct evidence of the first marriage (to Mary), and [A], [G], [L] collectively evidence the second (to Clarissa Wade), but none of these records are linked to the marriage conclusions on the profile. The marriage years recorded on the profile (year only, month missing) have no traceable source support in this audit.

**Marriage dates specifically.** No source gives a marriage date for either marriage. The years currently recorded appear to have been entered editorially. This is an open gap.

**All five residence conclusions.** FamilySearch's own profile checklist confirms that none of the five recorded residences has a tagged source. The census records read in this audit provide good support for residences in Au Sable (1850), Essex County NY (1865–1880), and Perinton, Monroe County NY (1910), but these records are not linked to the residence conclusions on the profile.

**Mother's identity.** The 1850 census [D] names the mother as Hannah (maiden name not given), while three death-era records name her as Jane Patterson. These are genuinely different names, and neither the life dates nor the maiden name of "Hannah" in the 1850 census are known from these records. Whether Hannah and Jane Patterson are the same person, or whether Jane was a stepmother, is unresolved and unsupported by any source currently on the profile that settles the question.

---

### 4. Overall Assessment of Profile Source Support

**Strengths.** The death event (date, place) is among the most strongly evidenced conclusions on the profile, with five independent sources converging on 16 August 1913, Burlington, Chittenden, Vermont. The birth year range is consistently supported at 1838–1839 by the majority of sources. The name, sex, and residence trajectory across census records are internally coherent. The second marriage to Clarissa Wade is confirmed by multiple independent source types.

**Weaknesses.** The specific birth day and month (30 November) rest on no traceable primary source visible in this audit and conflict with the only source giving a full date (Find a Grave, which says 31 January 1839). The first marriage (to Mary) has no tagged source despite direct evidence in the 1865 census. The second marriage has no tagged source despite evidence in three records. All five residence conclusions are untagged. The mother's name conflict (Hannah in 1850 vs. Jane Patterson in death records) is unresolved and not flagged anywhere on the profile. The 1870 census birth year conflict (implying 1840–1841) is flagged by FamilySearch but not corrected.

**Source quality by type.** The Vermont death registration ([A], [B], [K] represent multiple indexes of what is likely the same 1913 state death certificate) is the most authoritative source for the death event and for the informant-reported birth year and parentage. Census records are valuable for residence and household composition but are informant-reported for ages and birthplaces. The Find a Grave entry [J] is a single secondary source for the specific birth date and burial location; the date should not be treated as confirmed without a primary document. Source [L] (Helen McIntosh's 1943 death record) is secondary evidence for Edward's existence and his marriage to Clarissa Wade, but adds nothing about Edward's own vital events.

**Recommended research actions (in priority order):**

1. Re-read the original 1870 Vermont death certificate (the image is accessible through sources [A] and [C]) to verify the birth year the informant actually gave and to confirm the father's given name as it appears in manuscript — this would address both the birth year conflict and the "Jas" / "Joo" / "Jos." ambiguity.
2. Search for a New York or Vermont birth registration for Edward Tallman, born approximately 1838–1839, in Clinton County, New York (Peru township), to establish a primary birth date.
3. Tag the 1865 New York State Census [E] to the first marriage relationship on the profile.
4. Tag sources [A], [G], [L] to the second marriage relationship and tag the census records to the corresponding residence conclusions.
5. Search for a death record for Mary Tallman to establish the date of the first marriage's end and to confirm the mother's name on her death registration.
6. Search Joseph Tallman's records for a marriage to a "Hannah" and/or a "Jane Patterson" to resolve the mother conflict.

---

**Sources not individually read.** Approximately 15 additional sources appear on the profile, identified in the FamilySearch quality data as agreeing with the name and gender conclusions. By title they are Vermont Vital Records and Vermont Town Clerk entries (QPQV-662T, QPQG-F2GF, QPQL-F9N3, QPQX-DRDD, XF2X-BYV, XF4D-B9M, XFXS-8Y5, XFXS-886, 2V7M-6QM, KN9R-KC4, KF5F-WMS, KFTK-Z6N, XF2X-BYV, F8RW-X4N, F8R7-NW1). Based on their titles and collection coverage, most appear to be children's birth records where Edward appears as father, plus one or two additional indexes of the 1913 death registration. Their contents are not reported here because they were not read; none carry an artifact url that would bring them into the audit list automatically.

No project was found at /project, so no research log entry was written.

---

## Sources on Christian P. Hole (KD96-TV2) — 4 attached, 2 findings

---

### 1. "Minnesota Death Index, 1908–2002" — **Indexing Error**

The indexed death year is **1954**, but the profile records **1945**. The month and day (10 June), birth year (1875), birthplace (Norway), and death place (Erskine, Polk County, Minnesota) all match — this is almost certainly the right person with one mis-keyed year.

**Action:** Consult the original Polk County death certificate to confirm the correct year. If it reads 1945, submit an index correction through FamilySearch. **Keep the source attached** — it's the right record.

---

### 2. "Minnesota State Census, 1885" — **Misattributed; Detach**

The indexed person is a Christian Hole born **1852** in Norway, living in Aurdal, Otter Tail County, with wife Bergit and son Nils. Christian P. Hole was born in **1875** — he would have been about ten years old in 1885 and could not be this household head. The birth year, county, and wife's name all conflict.

This record also appears correctly attached to another tree person, **KD96-WX7** (Christian Hole, born 1852), where it fits on every point.

**Action:** **Detach this source** from Christian P. Hole's profile. It belongs to KD96-WX7, not to him.

---

### 3. Uploaded memory (funeral card/photograph) — *Cannot be verified*

This is a contributor-uploaded item with no indexed ARK. Its title references Christian P. Hole and 1945, which is consistent with the profile, but that title was supplied by the uploader. If the original death certificate is located and confirms 1945, this document may serve as a useful companion piece.

---

### Profile notes (not errors, but worth attention)
- The **marriage has no tagged sources**.
- A **marriage place is missing a city**.

---

**Summary:** One source has a mis-indexed death year (keep, correct the index); one source is attached to the wrong person entirely (detach, it belongs to KD96-WX7). The other two sources cannot be fully verified through indexed records alone.

Here is the source-evaluation agent's full audit of Christian P. Hole (KD96-TV2):

---

## Sources on Christian P. Hole (KD96-TV2) — 4 attached, 2 findings

---

### 1. Minnesota Death Index, 1908-2002 — **Indexing error**
**Link:** https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:HOLE-002

The index records the death year as **1954**; the profile records **1945** — a nine-year discrepancy. The day (10 June), month, name, birth year (1875), and death place (Erskine, Polk County, Minnesota) all match the profile. A single-field discrepancy where everything else fits is the classic signature of a transcription or indexing error.

**Action:** Obtain a copy of the original Minnesota death certificate to confirm the correct year, then use FamilySearch's index-correction path to fix the indexed year. Keep the source attached — it is good evidence with one suspect field.

---

### 2. Minnesota State Census, 1885 — **Misattributed; detach**
**Link:** https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:HOLE-003

This record names a Christian Hole born **1852** in Norway, living in **Aurdal, Otter Tail County**, with a wife named **Bergit** and a son Nils. Every field conflicts with the profile:

- **Birth year:** 1852 vs. 1875 on the profile — a 23-year gap, far beyond census variance.
- **County:** Otter Tail vs. Polk in every other source.
- **Spouse:** Bergit vs. Inger (named in the 1900 census).
- **Internal chronology:** If the profile's 1875 birth year were correct, this person would have been only ten years old in 1885 — far too young to appear as head of household with a spouse and a child born six years prior.

This record is already attached to **KD96-WX7**, a separate tree person named Christian Hole (born 1852, died 1919 in Otter Tail County) who matches the record on every point.

**Action:** Detach this source from KD96-TV2. It records an entirely different Christian Hole from a different generation and a different county.

---

### 3. Hole family photograph and funeral card (uploaded memory) — Could not fully verify

This is a contributor-uploaded document with no accessible record ID. Its title describes a funeral card for Christian P. Hole from Erskine, Minnesota, 1945 — which aligns with the **profile's** death year (1945) rather than the death index's erroneous 1954. This is relevant context for resolving finding #1, but the uploaded title may simply echo the tree. The card itself should be consulted alongside the original death certificate.

---

### Additional notes (profile checklist, not errors):
- The **marriage has no tagged sources**.
- A **marriage place** is missing a city.

---

**Summary:** One source has an indexing error in the death year (keep but correct); one source is misattributed to the wrong person entirely and should be detached. The uploaded funeral card is supportive but needs verification against the original certificate.

Here is the full audit of sources attached to **Cornelius Driscoll (GJ72-9WD)**, worst finding first:

---

## Sources on Cornelius Driscoll (GJ72-9WD) — 7 attached, 3 findings

---

### 1. ⚠️ Death date — source-vs-source conflict *(most severe)*

Two sources make contradictory claims about when Cornelius died:

- **"Quebec, Catholic Parish Registers, 1621–1979"** indexes the burial as **14 April 1878** and death as April 1878.
- **"Quebec, Civil Registration Deaths, 1867–1900"** indexes the death as **2 February 1885**.

A burial register and a civil death registration cannot both be right when they place the death nearly **seven years apart**. Both index the same name, birth year (1814), and birthplace (Ireland), so obvious misattribution cannot be ruled out from the indexes alone — one record may belong to a different Cornelius Driscoll in the Sherbrooke area.

**Next step:** Re-read both original records for additional identifying details (spouse, age at death, parents, occupation, parish) to anchor each firmly to the right person. Take this to conflict resolution with both original records in hand.

---

### 2. Marriage date — indexing error

- **"Quebec, Vital and Church Records (Drouin Collection), 1621–1968"** indexes the marriage date as **9 June 1845**; the profile records **9 June 1849**.

Day and month match exactly; only the year differs by four years — consistent with a misread digit in a handwritten register.

**Next step:** Re-read the original image (available within this collection). If the original reads 1849, correct the index. Keep the source attached.

---

### 3. 1851 residence place — ambiguous

- **"Census of Canada East, 1851"** indexes residence as **Melbourne, Canada East**; the profile records **Sherbrooke, Canada East**.

These are distinct places. No image is available within FamilySearch to check the original schedule.

**Next step:** Consult the original 1851 Canada East census schedule (microfilm or archival copy) to confirm which place the enumerator recorded.

---

### Could not check
One user-uploaded memory (Driscoll headstone photograph) carries no indexed record behind it. If the headstone bears dates relevant to the death-date conflict above, it is worth examining alongside both original records.

---

### Note on the 1861 census
The "Census of Canada, 1861" indexes a birth year of **1816** vs. the profile's **1814** — a two-year gap well within ordinary census-age variance. Not flagged as a finding.

### Finding 1 — "Minnesota Death Index, 1908–2002" — **Indexing Error**
The index records the death year as **1954**, but the profile says **1945** (a 9-year discrepancy). Every other field (name, birth year 1875, Norway, Erskine, Polk County, MN) matches perfectly. This is almost certainly a transcription slip in the index — the source itself belongs to this person. No image is available in the collection, so the next step is to locate the original Minnesota death certificate. If it confirms 1945, submit a correction through FamilySearch's index-correction process. **Keep the source attached.**

---

### Finding 2 — "Minnesota State Census, 1885" — **Misattributed Source**
This record is **not** about Christian P. Hole (KD96-TV2). The indexed person was born **1852** (the profile subject was born 1875 — he would have been only ~10 in 1885), lived in Aurdal, Otter Tail County, with a wife named Bergit and son Nils. None of that matches the subject.

Crucially, the tree already has another Christian Hole (KD96-WX7) whose profile records birth 1852 in Norway, residence in 1885 in Aurdal, Otter Tail County — an exact match to the census record. **This source belongs to KD96-WX7, not KD96-TV2.** It should be detached from KD96-TV2's profile.

---

### Could Not Fully Check
- An uploaded funeral-card/photograph memory item (SD-HOLE-D) has no indexed record behind it. Its title references the 1945 funeral in Erskine, MN, which is consistent with the profile, but a contributor-supplied title isn't independent evidence. Worth reviewing alongside the death certificate when that is located.

---

### Minor Profile Gaps (FamilySearch Suggestions)
- The marriage has no tagged sources.
- A marriage place is missing the city.

---

**Bottom line:** Detach the 1885 Minnesota State Census source and move it to KD96-WX7 (where it already belongs). Locate the original Minnesota death certificate to resolve the death-year discrepancy in the Death Index, and submit a correction if the certificate confirms 1945.

**"Minnesota Death Index, 1908–2002"**

**"Minnesota State Census, 1885"**

The indexed record names a Christian Hole born **1852 in Norway**, residing in **Aurdal, Otter Tail County, Minnesota** in 1885, with a wife named Bergit and a son Nils. Christian P. Hole was born in **1875** — that's a 23-year birth year gap — in a different county, with entirely different household members.

This record is also attached to **KD96-WX7** (another Christian Hole, born 1852 in Norway, died 1919 in Aurdal, Otter Tail, Minnesota), where every field matches perfectly.

**Next step:** **Detach this source** from KD96-TV2. It belongs to KD96-WX7.

---

- One **uploaded memory** (family photograph and funeral card) cannot be verified from an indexed ID; it names the 1945 death event, but uploader titles aren't independent corroboration.

### Finding 1 — Indexing Error (keep the source; correct the index)
**Minnesota Death Index, 1908–2002**

The index records the death year as **1954**; the profile says **1945**. Everything else agrees: name, birth year (1875, Norway), death place (Erskine, Polk County, Minnesota), and even the day and month (10 June). This is almost certainly a transcription error in the index, not a misattribution.

**Minnesota State Census, 1885**

The indexed entry names a Christian Hole born **1852** in Norway, residing in Aurdal, **Otter Tail County**, with a wife named **Bergit** and a child named Nils. The profile subject was born in **1875** (making him ~10 years old in 1885 — not a head of household), his wife's name is **Inger**, and his family was in Polk County, not Otter Tail. Three independent points of disagreement rule out a transcription-error explanation.

**Action:** Detach this 1885 census source from KD96-TV2. It belongs to KD96-WX7.
